analysis:
Examined the three changed files in this batch.

ProviderLoop+Testing.swift (head 514-523) adds two test seams:
- setSelectedModelRecoveryLoadOverrideForTesting sets selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride.
- awaitSelectedModelRecoveryAttemptForTesting awaits the in-progress attempt.
Unlike the DEBUG-only seams at lines 25-31 and 382-388, these are not #if DEBUG gated. They match the many other ungated internal seams in the file and are reachable only from in-module code or @testable import. ProviderLoop.swift 727-728 documents the override as nil in production. The supplied units show no production path that sets it.

ProviderLoop.swift (head 724-735, 897) adds state:
- selectedModelRecovery
- selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride
- savedEnabledModels, initialized from config enabled_models
- enabledModelsAtLastSwitch

ProviderLoop+Trust.swift (head 50-51, 54) adds three fields to the daemon state file:
- enabledModelsAtStart
- enabledModelsAtLastSwitch
- selectedModelRecovery report
These are local operator diagnostics: model ID lists and a recovery status. They are not consumer data (A-001), keys (A-002/A-003) or tokens (A-008), so no new disclosure is visible. The state file is written to the same local path as before.

No authorization, attestation, encryption or routing behavior changed in these units. clearConnectionAuthorization and handleTrustStatus are unchanged.

Open questions for integration (source not in this batch):
- ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery: does the no-eviction recovery load respect the add-on hold and model-load fence (TB-012, T-059, A-018)? Does it respect memory admission and the T-029 unload policy? Does it retry without bounds, creating an availability loop?
- Do savedEnabledModels and the policy refresh re-read the config file in a way that changes serving selection without a committed switch?
- Does the selectedModelRecoveryReport content contain only model IDs and status?
